hook: The founder of Sikhism, who taught one God and the equality of all people.

pages.x: Nanak was born in 1469 at Talwandi, near Lahore, in what is now Pakistan, to a Hindu family. As a boy he asked awkward questions. At the ceremony where he was to receive a sacred thread, he refused it and asked for a thread of kindness and truth that would never break.

Working as a storekeeper at Sultanpur, he went to bathe in a river and disappeared for three days. When he came back he said: "There is no Hindu and no Muslim", meaning all are equal before the one God. Sikhs see this as the beginning of their faith.
With his Muslim friend Mardana, who played the rabab, he travelled for more than twenty years, singing the hymns he composed, perhaps as far as Sri Lanka, Tibet, Mecca and Baghdad.

A story says that in Mecca he fell asleep with his feet pointing towards the Kaaba. An angry man dragged his feet the other way, and found that the Kaaba seemed to turn with them. Nanak said: then point my feet where God is not.

He settled at Kartarpur, a village he founded on the river Ravi, and farmed the land. There he began the langar, a free kitchen where everyone, of any caste or faith, sits together on the floor and shares a meal.

Guru Nanak founded Sikhism, followed today by about 25 million people. His hymns are in the Sikh holy book, and his teaching of one God, equality and service lives on in langars that feed millions every day.
pts: Taught one God and the equality of all people
Began the langar, the free community kitchen
